title: OASIS: Observation-Action Space Alignment via SE(3) Trajectory Prediction for Robotic Manipulation
claim: Prior policies feed intermediate representations unaligned with the action space into the decoder; ours predicts a pose trajectory to align them.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right columns, top-down flow, green 'aligned' bracket on ours
description: Four vertical columns separated by thin gray lines compare policy designs: Vanilla VLA, Feature-Enhanced VLA, World Action Model, and OASIS (Ours). Each column starts with the same three input icons: a scene photo, a blue speech bubble for language, and a robot arm. Arrows run downward through an intermediate representation to a rounded 'action decoder' box and then to '6-DoF actions'. The baseline columns show a multimodal feature grid, a grid plus spatial feature maps, and future visual state frames. Each baseline connects to the decoder with a dashed red arrow, marking a mismatch. The OASIS column differs: it has a 3D point-cloud box ('3D-aware representation') and a curved SE(3) trajectory with colored coordinate frames. Solid black arrows connect these to the decoder, and a green bracket labeled 'aligned' spans the last stages.
caption: Comparison of existing visuomotor policies and OASIS. VLA models and WAMs construct intermediate representations that are not aligned with the action space. OASIS instead aligns the intermediate representation with the action space via SE(3) trajectory prediction.
abstract: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models and world action models (WAMs) advance robotic manipulation by enriching intermediate representations with auxiliary spatial features or future visual-state prediction. However, these representations largely remain within the observation space and do not share the rigid-body geometry of the action space, forcing the action decoder to implicitly recover this geometry. We propose OASIS, a visuomotor policy that aligns the intermediate representation with the action space via $SE(3)$ end-effector trajectory prediction. OASIS couples a 3D-aware feature encoder that fuses vision-language and metric-depth features with an $SE(3)$ trajectory predictor that produces a camera-frame end-effector trajectory. Conditioned on the predictor's pose-supervised hidden states, the action decoder generates action chunks consistent with rigid-body motion. Across simulation and real-world experiments, OASIS outperforms VLA and WAM baselines in success rate and out-of-distribution generalization. Our project page is available at https://oasis-neurips.github.io.
